sanskrit: ata ūrdhvam idaṃ prāhuḥ strīparva karuṇodayam vilāpo vīrapatnīnāṃ yatrātikaruṇaḥ smṛtaḥ krodhāveśaḥ prasādaś ca gāndhārīdhṛtarāṣṭrayoḥ
english: After this, they speak of the Strī Parva, which arises from grief — where the lamentation of the wives of heroes is remembered as most pitiable, and the rage and subsequent composure of Gāndhārī and Dhṛtarāṣṭra are told.

sanskrit: yatra tān kṣatriyāñ śūrān diṣṭāntān anivartinaḥ putrān bhrātṝn pitṝṃś caiva dadṛśur nihatān raṇe
english: There they beheld those brave kṣatriyas who had met their fated end without retreating — their sons, brothers, and fathers slain on the battlefield.

sanskrit: yatra rājā mahāprājñaḥ sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ rājñāṃ tāni śarīrāṇi dāhayām āsa śāstrataḥ
english: There the greatly wise king, foremost among all upholders of dharma, performed the cremation of those royal bodies in accordance with scripture.

sanskrit: etad ekādaśaṃ proktaṃ parvātikaruṇaṃ mahat saptaviṃśatir adhyāyāḥ parvaṇy asminn udāhṛtāḥ
english: This eleventh parva has been described — deeply moving and great; twenty-seven chapters are enumerated in this parva.

sanskrit: ślokāḥ saptaśataṃ cātra pañcasaptatir ucyate saṃkhyayā bhāratākhyānaṃ kartrā hy atra mahātmanā praṇītaṃ sajjanamanovaiklavyāśrupravartakam
english: Seven hundred and seventy-five verses are said to be in it by count; the tale of the Bhārata composed here by that great-souled author moves the minds of good people to distress and to tears.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ śāntiparva dvādaśaṃ buddhivardhanam yatra nirvedam āpanno dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ghātayitvā pitṝn bhrātṝn putrān saṃbandhibāndhavān
english: After this comes the twelfth parva, the Śānti Parva, which increases wisdom — where king Yudhiṣṭhira, overcome with despair after having caused the slaughter of his elders, brothers, sons, in-laws, and kinsmen, finds peace.

sanskrit: śāntiparvaṇi dharmāś ca vyākhyātāḥ śaratalpikāḥ rājabhir veditavyā ye samyaṅ nayabubhutsubhiḥ
english: In the Śānti Parva, the duties spoken from the bed of arrows are expounded — those duties which kings who rightly desire knowledge of statecraft ought to know.

sanskrit: āpaddharmāś ca tatraiva kālahetupradarśakāḥ yān buddhvā puruṣaḥ samyak sarvajñatvam avāpnuyāt mokṣadharmāś ca kathitā vicitrā bahuvistarāḥ
english: There too are the duties in times of distress, which illuminate the causes relating to time — knowing which a person attains complete omniscience; and the varied, extensively elaborated dharmas of liberation are also told there.

sanskrit: dvādaśaṃ parva nirdiṣṭam etat prājñajanapriyam parvaṇy atra parijñeyam adhyāyānāṃ śatatrayam triṃśac caiva tathādhyāyā nava caiva tapodhanāḥ
english: This twelfth parva, dear to wise people, has been designated; to be known in this parva, O ascetics, are three hundred and thirty-nine chapters.

sanskrit: ślokānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi kīrtitāni caturdaśa pañca caiva śatāny āhuḥ pañcaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā
english: Fourteen thousand five hundred and twenty-five verses are said to be enumerated in it.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ tu vijñeyam ānuśāsanam uttamam yatra prakṛtim āpannaḥ śrutvā dharmaviniścayam bhīṣmād bhāgīrathīputrāt kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: After this is to be understood the excellent Anuśāsana Parva, where the Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira, restored to his natural disposition, hears the authoritative determination of dharma from Bhīṣma, the son of the Bhāgīrathī.

sanskrit: vyavahāro 'tra kārtsnyena dharmārthīyo nidarśitaḥ vividhānāṃ ca dānānāṃ phalayogāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ
english: Here all of civil conduct oriented toward dharma and artha is taught in its entirety, as are the various categories of merit arising from diverse kinds of gifts.

sanskrit: tathā pātraviśeṣāś ca dānānāṃ ca paro vidhiḥ ācāravidhiyogaś ca satyasya ca parā gatiḥ
english: Likewise the special distinctions of worthy recipients, the highest rule of giving, the practice of rules of conduct, and the supreme course of truth are all set forth.

sanskrit: etat subahuvṛttāntam uttamaṃ cānuśāsanam bhīṣmasyātraiva saṃprāptiḥ svargasya parikīrtitā
english: This Anuśāsana, containing many narratives and supreme, is where Bhīṣma's attainment of heaven is celebrated.

sanskrit: etat trayodaśaṃ parva dharmaniścayakārakam adhyāyānāṃ śataṃ cātra ṣaṭcatvāriṃśad eva ca ślokānāṃ tu sahasrāṇi ṣaṭ saptaiva śatāni ca
english: This thirteenth parva, which establishes the conclusions of dharma, contains one hundred and forty-six chapters and six thousand seven hundred verses.

sanskrit: tato 'śvamedhikaṃ nāma parva proktaṃ caturdaśam tat saṃvartamaruttīyaṃ yatrākhyānam anuttamam
english: Then comes the fourteenth parva named the Aśvamedhika; it contains the incomparable tale of Saṃvarta and Marutta.

sanskrit: suvarṇakośasaṃprāptir janma coktaṃ parikṣitaḥ dagdhasyāstrāgninā pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇāt saṃjīvanaṃ punaḥ
english: The acquisition of the treasury of gold is told there, as is the birth of Parīkṣit — who had previously been burned by the fire of a weapon and was brought back to life again by Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: caryāyāṃ hayam utsṛṣṭaṃ pāṇḍavasyānugacchataḥ tatra tatra ca yuddhāni rājaputrair amarṣaṇaiḥ
english: During the ritual progress, the horse released for the Pāṇḍava is followed, and battles with intolerant princes here and there are narrated.

sanskrit: citrāṅgadāyāḥ putreṇa putrikāyā dhanaṃjayaḥ saṃgrāme babhruvāhena saṃśayaṃ cātra darśitaḥ aśvamedhe mahāyajñe nakulākhyānam eva ca
english: There the peril of Dhanaṃjaya in battle against Babhruvāhana, son of Citrāṅgadā, born from a daughter given as an heir, is depicted; and the tale of Nakula in the great aśvamedha sacrifice is also told.

sanskrit: ity āśvamedhikaṃ parva proktam etan mahādbhutam atrādhyāyaśataṃ triṃśat trayo 'dhyāyāś ca śabditāḥ
english: Thus this Aśvamedhika Parva, full of great wonders, has been described; one hundred and thirty-three chapters are named in it.

sanskrit: trīṇi ślokasahasrāṇi tāvanty eva śatāni ca viṃśatiś ca tathā ślokāḥ saṃkhyātās tattvadarśinā
english: Three thousand three hundred and twenty verses have been counted by the seer of truth.

sanskrit: tata āśramavāsākyaṃ parva pañcadaśaṃ smṛtam yatra rājyaṃ parityajya gāndhārīsahito nṛpaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrāśramapadaṃ viduraś ca jagāma ha
english: After that is remembered the fifteenth parva called the Āśramavāsa, where the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having renounced his kingdom, together with Gāndhārī, went to his hermitage, and Vidura went with him.

sanskrit: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasthitaṃ sādhvī pṛthāpy anuyayau tadā putrarājyaṃ parityajya guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
english: Seeing him set forth, the virtuous Pṛthā also followed then, having given up the kingdom of her son, devoted to serving her elder.

sanskrit: yatra rājā hatān putrān pautrān anyāṃś ca pārthivān lokāntaragatān vīrān apaśyat punarāgatān
english: There the king saw his slain sons, grandsons, and other princes — heroes who had gone to another world — returned once more.

sanskrit: ṛṣeḥ prasādāt kṛṣṇasya dṛṣṭvāścaryam anuttamam tyaktvā śokaṃ sadāraś ca siddhiṃ paramikāṃ gataḥ
english: By the grace of the ṛṣi Kṛṣṇa (Dvaipāyana), having witnessed that incomparable marvel, he relinquished his grief and together with his wife attained the highest perfection.

sanskrit: yatra dharmaṃ samāśritya viduraḥ sugatiṃ gataḥ saṃjayaś ca mahāmātro vidvān gāvalgaṇir vaśī
english: There, taking refuge in dharma, Vidura attained a good state; and Saṃjaya too, that great minister, the learned son of Gavalgaṇa, the self-controlled one.

sanskrit: dadarśa nāradaṃ yatra dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ nāradāc caiva śuśrāva vṛṣṇīnāṃ kadanaṃ mahat
english: There dharma-king Yudhiṣṭhira saw Nārada, and from Nārada heard of the great destruction of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: etad āśramavāsākhyaṃ pūrvoktaṃ sumahādbhutam dvicatvāriṃśad adhyāyāḥ parvaitad abhisaṃkhyayā
english: This parva named the Āśramavāsa, described above, full of great marvels, is reckoned to contain forty-two chapters.

sanskrit: sahasram ekaṃ ślokānāṃ pañca ślokaśatāni ca ṣaḍ eva ca tathā ślokāḥ saṃkhyātās tattvadarśinā
english: One thousand five hundred and six verses have been counted by the seer of truth.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ nibodhedaṃ mausalaṃ parva dāruṇam yatra te puruṣavyāghrāḥ śastrasparśasahā yudhi brahmadaṇḍaviniṣpiṣṭāḥ samīpe lavaṇāmbhasaḥ
english: After this, learn of the terrible Mausala Parva, where those tiger-like men, who could endure the touch of weapons in battle, were crushed by the rod of brahmic power, near the salt sea.

sanskrit: āpāne pānagalitā daivenābhipracoditāḥ erakārūpibhir vajrair nijaghnur itaretaram
english: Intoxicated with drink in a drinking hall, driven on by fate, they struck one another with thunderbolts in the form of eraka reeds.

sanskrit: yatra sarvakṣayaṃ kṛtvā tāv ubhau rāmakeśavau nāticakramatuḥ kālaṃ prāptaṃ sarvaharaṃ samam
english: There, having wrought the total destruction, those two — Rāma and Keśava — did not transgress the time that had come, the time of universal dissolution, the equalizer.

sanskrit: yatrārjuno dvāravatīm etya vṛṣṇivinākṛtām dṛṣṭvā viṣādam agamat parāṃ cārtiṃ nararṣabhaḥ
english: There Arjuna, that bull among men, came to Dvāravatī emptied of the Vṛṣṇis and fell into profound despondency and great anguish.

sanskrit: sa satkṛtya yaduśreṣṭhaṃ mātulaṃ śaurim ātmanaḥ dadarśa yaduvīrāṇām āpāne vaiśasaṃ mahat
english: Having duly honored Śauri, the best of the Yadus, his own maternal uncle, he witnessed the great carnage of the Yadu heroes in the drinking hall.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ vāsudevasya rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ saṃskāraṃ lambhayām āsa vṛṣṇīnāṃ ca pradhānataḥ
english: He performed the funeral rites for the body of Vāsudeva and of great-souled Rāma, and for the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: sa vṛddhabālam ādāya dvāravatyās tato janam dadarśāpadi kaṣṭāyāṃ gāṇḍīvasya parābhavam
english: Taking the old and the young, the people from Dvāravatī, he then witnessed in that terrible calamity the failure of the Gāṇḍīva bow.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ caiva divyānām astrāṇām aprasannatām nāśaṃ vṛṣṇikalatrāṇāṃ prabhāvānām anityatām
english: He witnessed the unresponsiveness of all the divine weapons, the destruction of the wives of the Vṛṣṇis, and the impermanence of all powers.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nirvedam āpanno vyāsavākyapracoditaḥ dharmarājaṃ samāsādya saṃnyāsaṃ samarocayet
english: Having seen all this and overcome with dispassion, urged by the words of Vyāsa, he approached the dharma-king and resolved upon renunciation.

sanskrit: ity etan mausalaṃ parva ṣoḍaśaṃ parikīrtitam adhyāyāṣṭau samākhyātāḥ ślokānāṃ ca śatatrayam
english: Thus this Mausala Parva, the sixteenth, has been celebrated; eight chapters are named in it and three hundred verses.

sanskrit: mahāprasthānikaṃ tasmād ūrdhvaṃ saptadaśaṃ smṛtam yatra rājyaṃ parityajya pāṇḍavāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ draupadyā sahitā devyā siddhiṃ paramikāṃ gatāḥ
english: After that is remembered the seventeenth, the Mahāprasthānika, where the Pāṇḍavas, those bulls among men, having renounced their kingdom, together with the goddess Draupadī, attained the highest perfection.

sanskrit: atrādhyāyās trayaḥ proktāḥ ślokānāṃ ca śataṃ tathā viṃśatiś ca tathā ślokāḥ saṃkhyātās tattvadarśinā
english: In it three chapters are spoken and one hundred and twenty verses have been counted by the seer of truth.

sanskrit: svargaparva tato jñeyaṃ divyaṃ yat tad amānuṣam adhyāyāḥ pañca saṃkhyātāḥ parvaitad abhisaṃkhyayā ślokānāṃ dve śate caiva prasaṃkhyāte tapodhanāḥ
english: After that is to be known the Svarga Parva, divine and superhuman; five chapters are counted in this parva, O ascetics, and two hundred verses are reckoned.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśaivam etāni parvāṇy uktāny aśeṣataḥ khileṣu harivaṃśaś ca bhaviṣyac ca prakīrtitam
english: In this way eighteen parvas have been described in full; and among the supplements, the Harivaṃśa and the Bhaviṣyat are celebrated.

sanskrit: etad akhilam ākhyātaṃ bhārataṃ parvasaṃgrahāt aṣṭādaśa samājagmur akṣauhiṇyo yuyutsayā tan mahad dāruṇaṃ yuddham ahāny aṣṭādaśābhavat
english: All of this Bhārata has been narrated through the summary of the parvas; eighteen akṣauhiṇī armies came together out of desire for battle, and that great and terrible war lasted eighteen days.

sanskrit: yo vidyāc caturo vedān sāṅgopaniṣadān dvijaḥ na cākhyānam idaṃ vidyān naiva sa syād vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: A twice-born who might know the four Vedas together with their ancillaries and Upaniṣads, but does not know this epic tale — he would not truly be called learned.

sanskrit: śrutvā tv idam upākhyānaṃ śrāvyam anyan na rocate puṃskokilarutaṃ śrutvā rūkṣā dhvāṅkṣasya vāg iva
english: Having heard this narrative, nothing else that is fit to be heard pleases — just as after hearing the song of the male cuckoo, the harsh cry of the crow grates.

sanskrit: itihāsottamād asmāj jāyante kavibuddhayaḥ pañcabhya iva bhūtebhyo lokasaṃvidhayas trayaḥ
english: From this finest of itihāsas, the intellects of poets are born, just as from the five elements the three worlds come into being.

sanskrit: asyākhyānasya viṣaye purāṇaṃ vartate dvijāḥ antarikṣasya viṣaye prajā iva caturvidhāḥ
english: The Purāṇa exists within the domain of this narrative, O twice-born, just as the four kinds of beings exist within the domain of the sky.

sanskrit: kriyāguṇānāṃ sarveṣām idam ākhyānam āśrayaḥ indriyāṇāṃ samastānāṃ citrā iva manaḥkriyāḥ
english: This narrative is the refuge of all the qualities of action, just as the diverse activities of the mind are the refuge of all the senses.

sanskrit: anāśrityaitad ākhyānaṃ kathā bhuvi na vidyate āhāram anapāśritya śarīrasyeva dhāraṇam
english: Without taking refuge in this narrative, no story exists on earth — just as the sustaining of the body without taking recourse to food.

sanskrit: idaṃ sarvaiḥ kavivarair ākhyānam upajīvyate udayaprepsubhir bhṛtyair abhijāta iveśvaraḥ
english: This narrative is what all the foremost poets live by, as servants seeking advancement live by a nobly born lord.

sanskrit: dvaipāyanauṣṭhapuṭaniḥsṛtam aprameyaṃ; puṇyaṃ pavitram atha pāpaharaṃ śivaṃ ca yo bhārataṃ samadhigacchati vācyamānaṃ; kiṃ tasya puṣkarajalair abhiṣecanena
english: This immeasurable text issuing from the lips of Dvaipāyana — holy, purifying, sin-removing, and auspicious — whoever thoroughly studies the Bhārata as it is recited: what need has such a one of bathing in the waters of Puṣkara?

sanskrit: ākhyānaṃ tad idam anuttamaṃ mahārthaṃ; vinyastaṃ mahad iha parvasaṃgraheṇa śrutvādau bhavati nṛṇāṃ sukhāvagāhaṃ; vistīrṇaṃ lavaṇajalaṃ yathā plavena
english: This supreme narrative of great meaning, here set forth in this great summary of parvas — hearing it first, people enter it easily, as one crosses the vast salt sea with a vessel.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca janamejayaḥ pārikṣitaḥ saha bhrātṛbhiḥ kurukṣetre dīrghasatram upāste tasya bhrātaras trayaḥ śrutasena ugraseno bhīmasena iti
english: The Sūta said: Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit, was engaged in a long sacrifice at Kurukṣetra together with his brothers. His three brothers were Śrutasena, Ugrasena, and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: teṣu tat satram upāsīneṣu tatra śvābhyāgacchat sārameyaḥ sa janamejayasya bhrātṛbhir abhihato rorūyamāṇo mātuḥ samīpam upāgacchat
english: While they were seated at that sacrifice, a dog born of Saramā came there; struck by the brothers of Janamejaya, it went crying to its mother.

sanskrit: taṃ mātā rorūyamāṇam uvāca kiṃ rodiṣi kenāsy abhihata iti
english: His mother, seeing him crying, said: 'Why do you weep? By whom have you been struck?'

sanskrit: sa evam ukto mātaraṃ pratyuvāca janamejayasya bhrātṛbhir abhihato 'smīti
english: Thus addressed, he replied to his mother: 'I was struck by the brothers of Janamejaya.'

sanskrit: taṃ mātā pratyuvāca vyaktaṃ tvayā tatrāparāddhaṃ yenāsy abhihata iti
english: His mother replied to him: 'Clearly you must have done some wrong there, for which you were struck.'

sanskrit: sa tāṃ punar uvāca nāparādhyāmi kiṃ cit nāvekṣe havīṃṣi nāvaliha iti
english: He replied to her again: 'I have done no wrong at all — I did not look at the oblations, nor did I lick them.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tasya mātā saramā putraśokārtā tat satram upāgacchad yatra sa janamejayaḥ saha bhrātṛbhir dīrghasatram upāste
english: Hearing this, his mother Saramā, afflicted by grief for her son, went to that sacrifice where Janamejaya with his brothers was engaged in the long sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa tayā kruddhayā tatroktaḥ ayaṃ me putro na kiṃ cid aparādhyati kimartham abhihata iti yasmāc cāyam abhihato 'napakārī tasmād adṛṣṭaṃ tvāṃ bhayam āgamiṣyatīti
english: He was addressed there by her in anger: 'My son has done no wrong — for what reason was he struck? Because he was struck though he had done no harm, an unseen fear will come upon you.'

sanskrit: sa janamejaya evam ukto devaśunyā saramayā dṛḍhaṃ saṃbhrānto viṣaṇṇaś cāsīt
english: Thus addressed by Saramā, the divine dog, Janamejaya was greatly agitated and distressed.

sanskrit: sa tasmin satre samāpte hāstinapuraṃ pratyetya purohitam anurūpam anvicchamānaḥ paraṃ yatnam akarod yo me pāpakṛtyāṃ śamayed iti
english: When that sacrifice was completed, he returned to Hāstinapura and, seeking a suitable purohita, made great effort, thinking: 'One who can cleanse my sin.'

sanskrit: sa kadā cin mṛgayāṃ yātaḥ pārikṣito janamejayaḥ kasmiṃś cit svaviṣayoddeśe āśramam apaśyat
english: One day, Janamejaya son of Parīkṣit, while out hunting, saw a hermitage in a certain district of his own realm.

sanskrit: tatra kaś cid ṛṣir āsāṃ cakre śrutaśravā nāma tasyābhimataḥ putra āste somaśravā nāma
english: There a certain seer named Śrutaśravā dwelt; his beloved son, named Somaśravā, also lived there.

sanskrit: tasya taṃ putram abhigamya janamejayaḥ pārikṣitaḥ paurohityāya vavre
english: Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit, approached that son and solicited him for the office of purohita.

sanskrit: sa namaskṛtya tam ṛṣim uvāca bhagavann ayaṃ tava putro mama purohito 'stv iti
english: He bowed to that ṛṣi and said: 'Blessed one, let this your son be my purohita.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca bho janamejaya putro 'yaṃ mama sarpyāṃ jātaḥ mahātapasvī svādhyāyasaṃpanno mattapovīryasaṃbhṛto macchukraṃ pītavatyās tasyāḥ kukṣau saṃvṛddhaḥ samartho 'yaṃ bhavataḥ sarvāḥ pāpakṛtyāḥ śamayitum antareṇa mahādevakṛtyām asya tv ekam upāṃśuvratam yad enaṃ kaś cid brāhmaṇaḥ kaṃ cid artham abhiyācet taṃ tasmai dadyād ayam yady etad utsahase tato nayasvainam iti
english: Thus addressed, he replied: 'O Janamejaya, this son of mine was born of a serpent woman; he is a great ascetic, endowed with Vedic study, sustained by the power of my austerity, having grown in her womb which drank my seed. He is capable of cleansing all your sins — save for a deed against Mahādeva. But he has one secret vow: if any brahmin should ask him for anything, he must give it to that person. If you can accept this, then take him.'

sanskrit: tenaivam utko janamejayas taṃ pratyuvāca bhagavaṃs tathā bhaviṣyatīti
english: Thus urged, Janamejaya replied to him: 'Blessed one, so it shall be.'

sanskrit: sa taṃ purohitam upādāyopāvṛtto bhrātṝn uvāca mayāyaṃ vṛta upādhyāyaḥ yad ayaṃ brūyāt tat kāryam avicārayadbhir iti
english: Taking that purohita with him and returning, he said to his brothers: 'I have chosen this preceptor; whatever he says must be done without question.'

sanskrit: tenaivam uktā bhrātaras tasya tathā cakruḥ sa tathā bhrātṝn saṃdiśya takṣaśilāṃ pratyabhipratasthe taṃ ca deśaṃ vaśe sthāpayām āsa
english: Thus instructed by him, his brothers complied. Having so enjoined his brothers, he set out toward Takṣaśilā and brought that region under his control.

sanskrit: etasminn antare kaś cid ṛṣir dhaumyo nāmāyodaḥ tasya śiṣyās trayo babhūvur upamanyur āruṇir vedaś ceti
english: Meanwhile, there was a certain seer named Āyoda Dhaumya. He had three disciples: Upamanyu, Āruṇi, and Veda.

sanskrit: sa ekaṃ śiṣyam āruṇiṃ pāñcālyaṃ preṣayām āsa gaccha kedārakhaṇḍaṃ badhāneti
english: He sent one disciple, Āruṇi of Pāñcāla, saying: 'Go and stop up the breach in the field embankment.'

sanskrit: sa upādhyāyena saṃdiṣṭa āruṇiḥ pāñcālyas tatra gatvā tat kedārakhaṇḍaṃ baddhuṃ nāśaknot
english: Thus instructed by his teacher, Āruṇi of Pāñcāla went there but was unable to stop up that breach in the field embankment.

sanskrit: sa kliśyamāno 'paśyad upāyam bhavatv evaṃ kariṣyāmīti
english: Struggling and finding no solution, he thought: 'Let it be — I will do it thus.'

sanskrit: sa tatra saṃviveśa kedārakhaṇḍe śayāne tasmiṃs tad udakaṃ tasthau
english: He lay down there in the breach of the field embankment, and with him lying there, the water stopped.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid upādhyāya āyodo dhaumyaḥ śiṣyān apṛcchat kva āruṇiḥ pāñcālyo gata iti
english: Then one day the teacher Āyoda Dhaumya asked his disciples: 'Where has Āruṇi of Pāñcāla gone?'

sanskrit: te pratyūcuḥ bhagavatā eva preṣito gaccha kedārakhaṇḍaṃ badhāneti
english: They replied: 'He was sent by you yourself, saying: Go and stop up the breach in the field embankment.'

sanskrit: sa evam uktas tāñ śiṣyān pratyuvāca tasmāt sarve tatra gacchāmo yatra sa iti
english: Thus addressed, he said to those disciples: 'Then let us all go to where he is.'

sanskrit: sa tatra gatvā tasyāhvānāya śabdaṃ cakāra bho āruṇe pāñcālya kvāsi vatsaihīti
english: Going there, he called out to summon him: 'Ho, Āruṇi of Pāñcāla, where are you, my dear? Come here!'
